=============================

.. autoapi-nested-parse::

   Skeletonization, skeleton graph construction, pruning, paths, and topology.

Module Contents
---------------

.. py:data:: _NEI26

.. py:function:: skeleton_graph(skel: numpy.ndarray)

   Build the 26-connected voxel graph of a binary skeleton: ``(points, neighbor lists, degree)``.


.. py:function:: skeletonize_mask(mask_bool: numpy.ndarray) -> numpy.ndarray

   Thin a binary mask to its 1-voxel-wide skeleton (skimage medial-axis skeletonize).


.. py:function:: skeleton_tree_from_mask(mask_bool: numpy.ndarray, spacing=None, length_scale: float = 1.0) -> nvitk.measure.morpho.models.SkeletonTree

   Skeletonize *mask_bool*, optionally prune short terminal spurs, and build a :class:`SkeletonTree`.

   *length_scale* rescales the human-calibrated spur threshold for other
   species (see ``_meta.length_scale`` in the topology JSON).


.. py:function:: prune_short_terminal_spurs(skel: numpy.ndarray, max_len_mm: float, spacing=None) -> numpy.ndarray

   Erase terminal spur branches shorter than *max_len_mm* that end at a real branchpoint.

   Iterates to convergence since removing one spur can expose another; spurs that
   connect two true endpoints (not a branchpoint) are left alone so short vessels
   aren't deleted.


.. py:function:: skeleton_total_graph_length_mm(tree: nvitk.measure.morpho.models.SkeletonTree, spacing) -> float

   Sum of all edge lengths (mm) in the skeleton graph (each edge counted once).


.. py:function:: bfs_path_indices(neighbors: List[List[int]], src: int, dst: int) -> List[int]

   Breadth-first shortest (fewest-edges) path from *src* to *dst* in the skeleton graph.


.. py:function:: find_loop_branches(pts: numpy.ndarray, neighbors: List[List[int]], degree: numpy.ndarray)

   Detect simple donut/cycle topologies in a skeleton graph.

   :returns: nodes participating in at least one cycle.
             gateways: branchpoints where the loop connects to the rest of the tree.
             loops: list of (gateway_a, gateway_b, arm1_node_indices, arm2_node_indices).
   :rtype: cycle_core


.. py:function:: dijkstra_dist_from_root(tree: nvitk.measure.morpho.models.SkeletonTree, root: int, spacing) -> numpy.ndarray

   Physical (mm) shortest-path distance from *root* to every skeleton node.

   Plain O(n²) Dijkstra without a heap — skeleton graphs here are small enough
   that this is simpler and fast enough than a priority-queue implementation.


.. py:function:: skeleton_endpoints_and_path(skel: numpy.ndarray)

   Original fallback for unbranched vessels: longest endpoint-to-endpoint path.
